updatePolicy.note: Sources are checked each month. Comparable official crime figures are released quarterly, usually about four months after the period ends.

categories.label: All recorded crime
categories.description: All notifiable police-recorded offences excluding fraud. Anti-social behaviour incidents are not included.

categories.label: Violence
categories.description: Violence against the person, including homicide, violence with and without injury, stalking and harassment. Recording practices affect comparisons.

categories.label: Sexual offences
categories.description: Police-recorded rape and other sexual offences. Changes in reporting and recording can affect trends.

categories.label: Robbery
categories.description: Theft involving force or the threat of force against a person, including personal and business property. An April 2025 clarification of police counting rules increased the recording of business robbery during shop theft involving violence or threats. Changes in robbery and shoplifting across this date can reflect the recording change as well as changes in crime.

categories.label: Burglary
categories.description: Residential and non-residential burglary. Rates use resident population, rather than the number of households.

categories.label: Vehicle crime
categories.description: Theft of and from vehicles, vehicle interference and related vehicle offences.

categories.label: Theft from the person
categories.description: Theft directly from a person without force or threat of force, including pickpocketing.

categories.label: Shoplifting
categories.description: Police-recorded theft from shops. Counts depend on offences being reported to and recorded by police. From April 2025, clarified counting rules require shop theft involving violence or threats, including during escape, to be recorded as business robbery. This can affect year-on-year shoplifting comparisons spanning that date.

categories.label: Criminal damage & arson
categories.description: Recorded criminal damage to property and arson offences.

categories.label: Drug offences
categories.description: Drug possession and trafficking offences. Recorded totals are influenced by police activity.

categories.label: Weapons possession
categories.description: Possession of weapons offences. This is not a count of all knife-enabled crime.

categories.label: Public order
categories.description: Police-recorded public order offences, including offences involving fear or provocation of violence.

notes: The England and Wales reference includes British Transport Police; regional and territorial-force comparisons exclude it. London regional totals include City of London.

An April 2025 clarification of police counting rules increased the recording of business robbery during shop theft involving violence or threats. Changes in robbery and shoplifting across this date can reflect the recording change as well as changes in crime.
methodology: Counts describe police-recorded crime, rather than every crime that occurs. Reporting levels, recording practices and police activity affect comparisons and trends.
Each count covers a rolling 12-month period. Year-on-year change compares the count with the preceding rolling year ending in the same quarter.
Fraud and anti-social behaviour incidents are excluded. Weapons possession is not the same measure as knife-enabled crime.

Rates are calculated from exact ONS mid-year resident-population estimates, not inferred from rounded published rates. Historical rates use the latest available estimate at or before the year preceding each period end. Historical population estimates may be revised.
Crime histories sum four consecutive quarters from the latest Home Office revised open-data file. Latest and previous-year counts are reconciled against ONS Tables P1 and P4 before publication.
City of London counts remain visible, but its resident-based rates and rate rankings are suppressed. London regional totals include City of London.
This version covers England and Wales. Crime recording systems and offence definitions differ in Scotland and Northern Ireland.

areas.name: England and Wales
quality: Includes British Transport Police. Regional and territorial-force totals exclude British Transport Police, whose crimes cannot be assigned consistently to these areas.

areas.name: City of London
quality: Resident-population rates are suppressed, following the ONS treatment. The City has a large visiting and commuter population and is excluded from rate rankings.
